input.brief: Unfiltered with Wandia, a raw and unhurried Kenyan long-form podcast where real people share life stories on love, faith, money and purpose

direction.name: The split stage
direction.idea: Half the screen never moves. One side is a fixed photograph (or object, or product view) that stays in place for the whole visit; the other side is a calm scrolling column with everything you need to read. The fixed half keeps the feeling present while the reader gets on with the facts, like sitting in the room while reading the menu. As sections pass, the fixed image may quietly change to the one that matches.
direction.composition: Desktop: a two-column page, 50/50 or 45/55. One column is `position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh` and holds a single photograph filling it edge to edge, or the object centred on a flat field. The other column scrolls and holds all content in a single narrow measure (max 46ch) with comfortable padding (48–72px): name and one-line description first, then sections separated by generous space, then contact and footer. Headings in the scrolling column are modest (32–44px). The column grounds differ: photograph on one side, flat paper colour on the other, meeting at a clean vertical edge. On a phone the fixed half becomes a 60svh image at the top that stays sticky behind the first section, then releases.
direction.typography: A text-first setting: a readable serif or a calm sans at 17–19px, with one display size for the name. Left-aligned throughout.
direction.colour: The paper colour of the reading column is chosen against the photograph: a tone taken from its shadows or its lightest area. One ink, optionally one accent ink for links and the action.
direction.imagery: One excellent portrait-orientation photograph for the fixed half, plus three or four more that crossfade in as their sections arrive. Small inline photographs in the reading column are optional and should be few.
direction.richness: A full-height photograph always in view, against a quiet, well-set column of text.
direction.pitfalls: The reading column must be genuinely well typeset, since it is half the page. Do not put cards or grids in it. Check that the fixed image crops well at short viewport heights. In blind tests the commonest complaint was monotony: several screens of the same split with only the text changing. Change what the reading half holds from section to section (a list, a large figure, a table, a full-colour panel, a drawing) and let at least one section break the split and run full width.

hero.name: Anchored text, specimen half
hero.blueprint: The viewport is split exactly in half by two flat tones that meet at a clean vertical edge: the ground on the left, a palette colour on the right. Left half: the wordmark sits top-left on a 40px margin; the next two thirds of the height are empty; everything else is anchored bottom-left and ends 40px above the bottom edge: a headline on one or two lines at clamp(28px, 2.6vw, 40px), medium weight; one sentence at 18px in the soft ink, max 38ch; the single action as a solid rectangle. Right half: position: sticky; top: 0; height: 100svh. In its centre sits a square tile in a second palette colour, 450px wide (31vw) with a 24px radius, holding one cut-out item at 70% of the tile, object-fit: contain, mix-blend-mode: multiply on light fills. Under the tile's left corner the item's name and one fact sit at 15px. As the left column scrolls through the catalogue, the tile's item and colour swap to match the entry in view. One text link sits top-right on the colour field.
hero.mobile: The colour half comes first as a block 52svh tall holding the square tile at 62vw, centred, and stays sticky while the text slides over its lower edge. The text block follows on the ground: the headline at 7vw on two lines, the sentence at 16px, the action full width. The wordmark and one link sit on the top row over the colour.
hero.headline: A modest 3-6 word line at 28-40px, at most 40 characters; the object, not the type, carries the screen.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Photograph with figure tiles
sections.blueprint: A mosaic without gutters spanning the full width, about 66vw tall in total. A single photograph fills the left two-thirds at roughly 1:1 with object-fit: cover and square corners. The right third is split into two stacked flat colour tiles of equal height, in two palette colours that differ clearly in lightness as well as hue. Each tile carries one figure at clamp(56px, 5.6vw, 96px) in its top-left corner, 28px in from the edges, with a two-line caption at 17px directly beneath it; the rest of the tile is empty colour, which is the point. Photograph and tiles touch, with no gaps and no rounding. The heading, two to four words at 32–40px, sits above the mosaic's left edge with 40px beneath, or is left out when the section follows a text page whose title already introduces it. Never add a third tile; with three figures choose another layout.
sections.mobile: The photograph comes first, full-bleed at 4:3. The two colour tiles follow side by side as squares, each 50vw, with the figure at 13vw top-left and the caption at 15px beneath. No gaps between any of the three pieces.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: Title torn at the seam
sections.blueprint: A wrapper about 95svh tall per project holds a sticky stage of 100svh, split at exactly 50vw into two portrait panes of 720×900px, `object-fit: cover`, square corners, no gap: two different pictures or loops of the same project (the whole and a detail, before and after). The project's title sits on the seam, centred on x 720 at the optical middle: capitals in a heavy face at clamp(96px, 11vw, 160px), leading 0.8, tracking -0.04em, at most two lines, in one light colour chosen per project. It is set twice inside the one heading element, the second copy `aria-hidden`, each copy clipped to its own half with `clip-path: inset(0 50% 0 0)` and `inset(0 0 0 50%)`. Directly under it, centred, the discipline and year at 16px and a text link with an arrow at 16px. While a project crosses the stage, the left pane and left half-title travel up and the right pane and right half-title travel down (panes ±20svh, title ±30svh, on a scroll-linked timeline), so the name tears at the seam and lines up exactly when the project is centred. The section's two-word heading sits at clamp(28px, 2.4vw, 36px) in the stage's top-left corner, 32px in. Four to eight projects; the stage releases after the last. Under reduced motion the halves stay aligned and the projects change by crossfade.
sections.mobile: Keep the split: two strips 195px wide running the full height of the screen with the same opposing travel. The title drops to 12.5vw on the seam, at most two lines, with the discipline line and the link under it at 16px; give the link a 44px hit area.

sections.name: Drag row of mixed modules
sections.blueprint: One horizontal row, 68svh tall, running off both viewport edges with 12px gaps, draggable and scrollable sideways (`overflow-x: auto`, `scroll-snap-type: x proximity`, scrollbar hidden). The row is built from three module types: a tall single image at 3:4 filling the row height; a column of two stacked 4:3 images sharing the height with a 12px gap; and a wide 16:10 landscape at full height. Sequence for nine photographs: tall, stacked pair, wide, stacked pair, tall, wide. The row starts 6vw in from the left, so the first module is whole and the last visible one is cut by the right edge. A heading of two or three words at 28–36px sits 32px above the row's left start; the count of photographs sits at the right margin on the same baseline. No captions and no arrows. Inside a narrow reading column the same row runs 300px tall and is cut by the column's edge.
sections.mobile: The row is 62svh tall with 8px gaps and starts 20px in. Modules are sized so one and a third are visible: tall images 72vw wide, stacked pairs 64vw wide, landscapes 88vw wide at reduced height and centred vertically. Scroll snapping aligns each module to the left margin.

sections.name: Prices like a menu
sections.blueprint: Prices set the way a good menu sets them. A heading of two to three words at 32–40px sits in columns 1–3. Columns 5–12 hold the list in two text columns with a 64px gap. Items are grouped under plain group names at 24px in medium weight with 48px above each group. Each item is a row: the name at 19px on the left, the price at the same size on the right on the same baseline, with tabular figures and the currency sign shown only once per group; beneath the name, one line of description at 16px in the softer ink, no wider than 36ch. Rows are 22px apart. Name and price are joined only by empty space (flex with `justify-content: space-between`), with no dot leaders and no lines. One small photograph (4:5, three columns wide) may sit under the heading in the left zone.
sections.mobile: One column. The heading at 28px, then the photograph at 60% width if used. Each item keeps name left and price right on one line at 17px, with its description beneath in the softer ink. Group names at 20px with 40px above.

sections.name: Photo strip, three-cell bar
sections.blueprint: A saturated flat field about 80svh tall. Across the top, 48px from the section edge, a strip of small photographs runs off both sides: all 150px tall at differing widths (3:4, 1:1, 3:2 in turn), 8px gaps, ten or more, drifting slowly as a marquee. A heading of two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px) sits 72px below the strip at the left margin. 40px below the heading, the newsletter or booking form is one bar spanning the content width, 96px tall, divided into three equal cells with 8px gaps. Each cell is a filled block in a tone one step from the field with one radius: the first two are inputs (name, email) with placeholder text centred at 18px, the third is the submit action in the inverse colours with its word centred. Focus changes a cell's fill to the lightest tone. Small print at 13px sits under the first and third cells.
sections.mobile: The strip is 110px tall and scrolls by touch. The heading follows at 9vw. The three cells stack as full-width filled blocks 60px tall with 8px gaps, the submit block last. Small print sits beneath the stack, left-aligned.

sections.name: Questions beside a tall photograph
sections.blueprint: One field in a deep or pale flat tone, split 5 to 7. Left, columns 1–5: a heading of two to four words at 36–44px; under it the three or four practical facts people ask first (address, times, how to arrive) as plain lines at 18px; then five or six questions as an accordion with no lines between rows, only 28px of space. Each question is a `<summary>` at 20px with a small chevron drawn from two 2px strokes at its right; the open answer sits beneath at 17px in the softer ink, on the same left edge. One filled button and one text link close the column. Right, columns 7–12: a tall photograph (3:4) that bleeds off the top edge of the section and stops 80px short of the bottom, with a second, square photograph a third of its width overlapping its lower-left corner by 40px.
sections.mobile: The tall photograph leads at full width, 4:5, with the square one overlapping its bottom-right corner at 38% width. Heading at 30px, facts at 17px, then the accordion at full width with 24px between questions and 44px touch targets. Button full width at the end.

sections.name: Last photograph, text beside
sections.blueprint: A final full-bleed photograph, 100vw by 90svh, chosen so its subject sits in the left half and its right half is calm. All text is confined to the right half and never crosses the centre line: in columns 8–12, anchored to the lower third, a closing line of three to five words at about 3.4vw in a light weight, a paragraph of two or three lines at 17px, and one filled button in the paper colour with ink text, about 52px tall. If the image behind the text is not calm enough, darken the whole photograph slightly with `filter: brightness(0.8)` rather than laying a panel behind the words. The section butts directly against a footer in one solid colour, so the photograph's bottom edge is a hard line. No logo, no second action.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100vw by 70svh, cropped to keep its subject. The text leaves the image and sits beneath it on the footer's solid colour: closing line at 28px, paragraph at 17px, full-width button. Image and colour meet at a hard edge.

references.name: Rafael Derolez
references.idea: A portfolio as a phone carousel: a fixed text rail on the left narrates whichever phone-shaped screen is centred on the right.
references.hero: Dark charcoal page split by a vertical hairline at 30% width. Left rail: a 55px header row with name, slash and current section as a breadcrumb in 16px sans, plus a small cobalt ticket-shaped hire button with a perforated divider and arrow; below a hairline, four short paragraphs of 16px grey text with white links, top-aligned, leaving the lower 40% of the rail empty. Right 70%: three phone-proportioned frames with large rounded corners in a row; the centre one upright, full brightness and about 680px tall, the outer two smaller, dimmed and rotated in perspective toward the centre.
references.type: Suisse at a single 16px size, weight 400, for everything; hierarchy comes only from grey versus white and from the breadcrumb. The one larger setting is a bold two-word line inside the blue contact card. No display type at all.
references.colour: #18181b #030303 #969696 #173ded #ffffff — Zinc-black field with grey text and white for links and the active breadcrumb. Cobalt blue appears only on the hire button and contact card; all other colour comes from the app screenshots.
references.imagery: Phone-shaped frames with large corner radius holding app screens, a selfie and short videos; side frames are dimmed to about 40% and tilted in 3D like a cover-flow.
references.layout: Single viewport, no page scroll: a fixed 432px text rail with 32px padding and a media stage filling the rest. Scrolling advances the carousel and replaces the rail's text; hairlines separate rail, header and stage. On mobile the stage stacks above the rail.

sections.description: Same two-part frame. The breadcrumb's last word changes to the project name; under the header sit three tiny grey meta tags (employer, platform), then two paragraphs. On the stage the centred phone shows the product screen at full brightness while neighbours show the previous and next items dimmed and tilted, so the carousel works as both navigation and preview.

In the rail, a cobalt card shaped like a ticket with notched sides: tiny labels top-left and top-right, a large bold two-word heading, name and local time in small text, then a perforated lower strip with email at left and a copy button at right. Under it, a career list: company in white with dates in small grey on one line, role on the next, and a small arrow at the far right of each row.

steal: Use a breadcrumb (name / current item) as the only heading and update its last word as the content changes.
Show work in device-shaped frames arranged as a cover-flow, with neighbours dimmed and tilted so the next item is always previewed.
Shape the contact card like a ticket with notches and a perforated strip so the one accent-colour element feels like an object.

references.name: Le Petit Bleu
references.idea: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.
references.hero: Viewport split 50/50 with 12px gaps. Left: a cream panel with a thin pale-teal outline and rounded corners. Inside, a second outlined box is the nav bar: two-line hamburger left, teal brush-script logo about 300px wide centred, a caps order link right. Below, a two-line light serif headline at about 3.5vw, centred, in teal, then two centred stacks, each a bold caps label, a serif line and a solid teal button wrapped in a second thin outline. Right: a full-height rounded photo of a striped booth, with an outlined hours bar across its top, three slide dots bottom-left and a white address card bottom-right.
references.type: Self Modern, a light bookish serif, for headline and 15px body; Matter SQ bold caps for labels and buttons; Archive Mono Pro typewriter caps for menu rows; a brush-script logo. Section titles are tall condensed serif caps sized so four to seven letters fill the column.
references.colour: #fcfbf7 #13a7b2 #058599 #cfe5e7 #e9b81f — Cream paper and a single teal used for every word, rule, outline and button; no black anywhere. Yellow, floral reds and marble enter only through the interior photographs.
references.imagery: Bright, saturated interior and food photographs; the right-hand panel is a full-height slideshow with rounded corners. Small food shots sit in a horizontal strip, and a fine line drawing of the shopfront with one teal awning fills a card.
references.layout: The left half scrolls as a stack of outlined cream cards (full-width or two-up) with 12px gaps while the right half stays fixed. Card contents are centred. A sticky nav card rides over the stack. On mobile the photo becomes the hero card's background.

sections.description: A card containing only the section word in tall condensed serif caps, teal, sized so its four letters fill the column edge to edge. Below it, a stack of full-width outlined rows about 36px high, each with a category name in typewriter mono caps at left and a thin plus sign at right, separated by 6px gaps. Above the title: a ticker row of tiny caps and a strip of four small food photos with rounded corners.

The same giant condensed title treatment, then centred serif paragraphs in teal with underlined links in a narrow measure of about 280px. Further down, a landscape photo of the two proprietors with a centred two-line caption in tiny sans, followed by more centred paragraphs. All of it lives in the left half while the right photo panel has advanced to a shelf-wall image.

A header row with a tiny bold caps label at left and a script follow-us link with arrow at right, then three portrait images (about 3:5) with 12px rounded corners in a row, the third cropped by the column edge to imply a carousel. Directly below, the next giant section title begins and is cropped by the viewport.

steal: Print everything in one brand ink on cream, including body text, rules and buttons, and let photographs supply the other colours.
Wrap buttons and panels in a second thin outline offset by a few pixels to get a printed-ticket feel.
Keep a tall photo panel fixed on one half and scroll a stack of cards on the other, swapping the photo as sections change.

references.name: 21 Hrs On The Moon
references.idea: An explorable Apollo 11 landing site: a title screen where the word MOON sets behind the lunar horizon, then a draggable top-down surface map with hotspots and a mission timeline.
references.hero: Black starfield framed by thin bronze corner brackets; three small round icon buttons top-left. A centred composition 72% wide sits between two thin rules. The upper rule is interrupted by a small bold caps kicker; beneath it the four-letter title in bold geometric caps at 20.8vw spans the full width, light grey fading to transparent at its base. A grey cratered sphere rises from the bottom, its curved horizon overlapping the lower quarter of the letters. On the sphere: a two-line centred white sentence, with a mono-labelled mission name at far left and year at far right above the lower rule. A bracketed mono button sits centred at 82% height.
references.type: Futura Std Bold in uppercase at 300px with -0.03em tracking for the title, the same face near 28px for the kicker and 20px for the sentence; Akkurat Mono in tiny uppercase for labels, the button and map annotations. Roughly a 15x jump from title to sentence.
references.colour: #020202 #262626 #d8d8d8 #8a7361 #ffffff — Black and lunar greys with white type. A muted bronze appears only in the HUD brackets and translucent wedge markers on the map; archival photo thumbnails add small spots of colour.
references.imagery: A real-time 3D moon: curved horizon on the title screen, then a full-screen top-down cratered surface lit from one side. Small archival photos appear as thumbnail hotspots with bracketed corners; icons sit in outlined circles and squares.
references.layout: A single-screen application rather than a scrolling page: a centred title card, then a draggable map filling the viewport with hotspots at fixed coordinates. HUD brackets, icon buttons at top-left and a timeline ruler along the bottom persist throughout.

sections.description: Full-viewport top-down lunar surface in dark grey with fine crater relief. About ten hotspots are scattered over it: outlined circular icons for panoramas, each with a translucent bronze wedge showing the camera's field of view; small square icons for experiments; two photo thumbnails with corner brackets. Each has a tiny mono caps label to its right. One landmark gets a larger bold geometric caps label with a small triangle above it. A tiny mono hint sits top-centre.

Pinned along the bottom, a horizontal ruler spanning about 75% of the width: a thin baseline with short vertical ticks dividing eight equal segments, each labelled in two lines of tiny mono caps, a small triangle marking the current position and a clock readout at the left end. The current landmark's name in bold caps sits beneath it, half-cropped by the bottom edge of the screen.

steal: Let a 3D or photographic object physically overlap the bottom of giant title letters and fade the letters to transparent there, so the type sits inside the scene rather than on top of it.
Interrupt a thin horizontal rule with the small first line of the title, then close the block with a second rule carrying two labelled facts at its left and right ends.
Frame the viewport with four thin corner brackets in a muted metallic colour to turn a full-screen scene into a viewfinder.
references.media: The hero is all picture: a starfield and a rising moon sphere over the lower ~55%, with the title sunk into its horizon. After landing, a draggable top-down terrain map fills the whole screen, with 120x90 archival photo thumbnails as pins and translucent field-of-view wedges; no video on the surface, as footage and panoramas open from the hotspots.
references.motion: There is no document scroll: the first wheel step plays a landing in which the terrain lights up and the hotspots arrive in a stagger, labels after their icons, and from then on the wheel does nothing and the map is dragged instead. HUD items fade in and out on a uniform 400ms, with one opacity .3s cubic-bezier(.61,1,.88,1); no GSAP, and the page took 38s to reach network idle.
